proposed.explanation:
No, Telecom Egypt (ETEL) is not bigger than Talaat Moustafa Group Holdings (TMGH) by either measure. On FY2025 net profit, ETEL earned 578,063,000 EGP versus TMGH's 18,201,981,482 EGP – TMGH is roughly 31 times larger. On total consolidated equity at 31 Dec 2025, ETEL stands at 63,687,826,000 EGP versus TMGH's 157,708,140,765 EGP – TMGH is about 2.5 times larger. So TMGH is the bigger company on both counts.

Your stated goal is to add a bigger company, and you already hold 200 shares of TMGH, the larger of the two. ETEL does not meet the 'bigger company' criterion, so there is no evidence-based reason to deploy your 20,000 EGP cash into ETEL right now. I recommend keeping the cash for now and looking for a company that genuinely satisfies your size requirement. If you simply want to increase your position in the bigger company you already own, that would be a separate decision (buying more TMGH), but the evidence provided here does not include a valuation or growth outlook that would justify a specific buy size for TMGH either.

Risks and uncertainty: The figures are single-year snapshots; a one-year comparison does not capture cyclicality, one-off items, or the quality of earnings. ETEL's FY2025 net profit (578 M EGP) is dramatically lower than its FY2024 figure (10,111 M EGP), which could signal a one-off charge or a structural change – without further detail I cannot judge which. TMGH's 2024 figures are restated, so the year-on-year growth rate should be read with caution. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
